name: Rod of Channeling
summary: In the Wetlands, the Rod of Channeling is carried by Dragonmaw spellcasters. Warlocks seeking to summon a felhunter gather three for Strahad Farsan's acolytes to steady the ritual circle in Ratchet.

sections.title: Instruments of Binding
sections.body: Warlocks need more than willpower to bind a volatile felhunter. Strahad Farsan asks for three matched rods so his acolytes can channel magic together and steady the summoning circle while the warlock binds the beast. Dragonmaw darkcasters carry these rods for their own workings. Bonewarders and shadowwarders bear them at Angerfang Encampment and in the surrounding Wetlands ruins. Combat leaves the rods worn and nicked, but they still focus chaotic nether energy.

faq.q: What is the Rod of Channeling used for?
aliases: why do i need rod of channeling
faq.answer: The rods go to Strahad Farsan above Ratchet. His acolytes use them to channel and steady the circle needed to summon and bind a hostile felhunter.

faq.q: Where can Rods of Channeling be found?
aliases: where to get rods of channeling
faq.answer: Dragonmaw spellcasters carry the rods in the Wetlands, especially Dragonmaw Bonewarders and Shadowwarders around Angerfang Encampment.

faq.q: Why does Strahad need three rods?
faq.answer: Strahad's acolytes assist with the felhunter summoning ritual. Each needs a focus to hold the conduit steady while the warlock subdues the beast.

faq.q: Why are the Dragonmaw using these rods?
faq.answer: The Dragonmaw clan uses the rods in its dark shamanism and shadowcraft, remnants of the Old Horde. Its bonewarders and shadowwarders channel curses, necromancy, and shadow magic in their ongoing territorial wars in the Wetlands.

angles.text: As a warlock, you gather three Rods of Channeling during the Tome of the Cabal trials. They help contain the ritual as you bind your first felhunter.
